# Data Split

```{r}
# 
# db_res %>%
#   select(-c(ID, Group)) %>%
#   ggpairs() # Así se ve la correlación entre variables. Es importante no tomar en cuenta 

# Hay otras formas de hacer esto. Yo solo use esta función y quité las variables que eran redundantes, pero es que mis datos tenían variables que eran super dependientes unas de otras. El señorcito explica muchas cosas aquí que no he terminado de entender https://hbiostat.org/rmsc. En este es específico de bioestadñistica https://hbiostat.org/bbr. Estoy tratando de leer sus cosas. Si querés mejor no uses lo de redun().
#  Creating repeated CV folds
set.seed(123)

full_db <- db

test_db <- db %>%
  group_by(Group) %>%
  slice_sample(n = 1) %>%
  ungroup()

db <- db %>%
  anti_join(test_db, by = "ID")

X <- db %>% select(-ID, -Group)
y <- db$Group



folds <- createMultiFolds(
  y = y,
  k = 3,
  times = 10
)

fold_data <- vector("list", length(folds))

for (i in seq_along(folds)) {

  train_idx <- folds[[i]]
  valid_idx <- setdiff(seq_len(nrow(db)), train_idx)

  train_data <- db[train_idx, ]
  valid_data <- db[valid_idx, ]


  # -------------------------
  # redun ONLY on training
  # -------------------------

  red_vars <- redun(
    as.matrix(
      train_data %>%
        select(-ID, -Group)
    )
  )

  selected_vars <- red_vars$In


  # -------------------------
  # Selected variables
  # -------------------------

  train_X <- train_data %>%
    select(ID, Group, all_of(selected_vars))

  valid_X <- valid_data %>%
    select(ID, Group, all_of(selected_vars))


  # -------------------------
  # PCA ONLY on training
  # -------------------------

  pca_fit <- prcomp(
    train_X %>% select(-ID, -Group),
    scale. = TRUE
  )


  # -------------------------
  # PCA scores
  # -------------------------

  train_pca <- predict(
    pca_fit,
    train_X %>% select(-ID, -Group)
  )

  valid_pca <- predict(
    pca_fit,
    valid_X %>% select(-ID, -Group)
  )


  # -------------------------
  # Save everything
  # -------------------------

  fold_data[[i]] <- list(
    train_idx = train_idx,
    valid_idx = valid_idx,
    train_X = train_X,
    valid_X = valid_X,
    red_vars = red_vars,
    selected_vars = selected_vars,
    pca_fit = pca_fit,
    train_pca = train_pca,
    valid_pca = valid_pca
  )
}
```

# Defining model training functions

```{r}

calculate_fold_metrics <- function(results, Group_levels) {

  fold_metrics <- lapply(seq_along(results), function(i) {

    x <- results[[i]]

    obs  <- factor(x$obs,  levels = Group_levels)
    pred <- factor(x$pred, levels = Group_levels)

    cm <- confusionMatrix(
      data = pred,
      reference = obs
    )

    # Group-specific metrics
    precision <- cm$byGroup[, "Pos Pred Value"]
    recall    <- cm$byGroup[, "Sensitivity"]

    f1 <- 2 * precision * recall / (precision + recall)

    # MultiGroup AUC
    auc_result <- multiGroup.roc(
      response = obs,
      predictor = as.matrix(x[, Group_levels])
    )

    auc <- as.numeric(auc_result$auc)

    # Macro averages
    macro_precision <- mean(precision, na.rm = TRUE)
    macro_recall    <- mean(recall, na.rm = TRUE)
    macro_f1        <- mean(f1, na.rm = TRUE)

    data.frame(
      Resample = paste0("Fold", i),
      Accuracy = unname(cm$overall["Accuracy"]),
      Precision = macro_precision,
      Recall = macro_recall,
      F1 = macro_f1,
      AUC = auc
    )
  })

  bind_rows(fold_metrics)
}


# Holi! Esto lo hice para plotear las predicciones de los modelos. No creo que sea necesario. Tenía que transformar a principal components porque necesitaba 2 dimensiones. chat me ayudó.

make_bound_plot <- function(mod, dat, pcx = 1, pcy = 2, alg) {
  set.seed(2024)  # Ensure reproducibility in PCA transformation

  preproc <- preProcess(dat[-c(1,2)], method = c("pca"))
  pca_transformed <- predict(preproc, dat[-c(1,2)])
  pca_transformed <- data.frame(pca_transformed, Group = dat$Group)

  colnames(pca_transformed)[pcx] <- "X"
  colnames(pca_transformed)[pcy] <- "Y"

  # Create a grid of points in the PCA-transformed space
  x_min <- min(pca_transformed$X) - 1
  x_max <- max(pca_transformed$X) + 1
  y_min <- min(pca_transformed$Y) - 1
  y_max <- max(pca_transformed$Y) + 1

  # Generate grid points
  grid <- expand.grid(X = seq(x_min, x_max, length.out = 100),
                      Y = seq(y_min, y_max, length.out = 100))

  # Combine the grid with zeros for other components
  grid_full <- data.frame(matrix(0, nrow = nrow(grid), ncol = ncol(pca_transformed)-1))
  colnames(grid_full) <- colnames(pca_transformed)[-ncol(pca_transformed)]
  grid_full[, c(pcx, pcy)] <- grid

  # Inverse transform the grid to the original feature space
  inverse_pca <- function(pca_model, pca_data) {
    center <- pca_model$mean
    scale <- pca_model$std
    rotation <- pca_model$rotation
    
    # Calculate the original data matrix
    original_matrix <- as.matrix(pca_data) %*% t(rotation)
    
    # Re-scale and re-center
    original_matrix <- sweep(original_matrix, 2, scale, `*`)
    original_matrix <- sweep(original_matrix, 2, center, `+`)
    
    return(as.data.frame(original_matrix))
  }

  # Perform inverse PCA transformation on the grid
  grid_original <- inverse_pca(preproc, grid_full)
  colnames(grid_original) <- colnames(dat[-c(1,2)])

  # Predict on the original feature space
  grid_original$Group <- predict(mod, grid_original, type = "raw")
  grid_original$Group <- relevel(grid_original$Group, ref = "Control")

  # Plot the decision boundary
  ggplot() +
    geom_point(data = pca_transformed, aes(x = X, y = Y, color = Group), size = 2) +
    geom_tile(data = grid, aes(x = X, y = Y, fill = grid_original$Group), alpha = 0.3) +
    labs(title = paste(alg, "Decision Boundary on PCA-projected Data"),
         x = paste("Principal Component", pcx),
         y = paste("Principal Component", pcy)) +
    theme_minimal() +
    scale_color_manual(name = "Reference", labels = levels(pca_transformed$Group), values = c("#a39b9b",  "#67c7c5", "#f2de79")) +
    scale_fill_manual(name = "Prediction", labels = levels(pca_transformed$Group), values = c("#a39b9b",  "#67c7c5", "#f2de79"))
}
```

# Multinomial logistic regression with neural networks

```{r}
ctrl_none <- trainControl(
  method = "none"
)

nn_models <- vector("list", length(fold_data))

for (i in seq_along(fold_data)) {

  dat <- fold_data[[i]]

  nn_models[[i]] <- train(
    x = dat$train_X %>% select(-ID, -Group),
    y = dat$train_X$Group,
    method = "rf",
    trControl = ctrl_none
  )
}

nn_results <- vector("list", length(fold_data))

for (i in seq_along(fold_data)) {

  dat <- fold_data[[i]]
  model <- nn_models[[i]]

  pred <- predict(
    model,
    newdata = dat$valid_X %>% select(-ID, -Group)
  )

  prob <- predict(
    model,
    newdata = dat$valid_X %>% select(-ID, -Group),
    type = "prob"
  )

  nn_results[[i]] <- data.frame(
  ID = dat$valid_X$ID,
  obs = dat$valid_X$Group,
  pred = pred,
  prob
)
}

nn_metrics <- lapply(seq_along(nn_results), function(i) {

  metric_data <- nn_results[[i]] %>%
    select(ID, obs, pred, all_of(levels(db$Group))) %>%
    as.data.frame()

  multiGroupSummary(
    data = metric_data,
    lev = levels(db$Group),
    model = nn_models[[i]]
  )
})

nn_metrics <- bind_rows(
  nn_metrics,
  .id = "fold"
)

conf_matrices_nn <- lapply(nn_results, function(x) {
  confusionMatrix(
    data = x$pred,
    reference = x$obs
  )
})

names(conf_matrices_nn) <- paste0("Fold_", seq_along(conf_matrices_nn))


all_nn_results <- bind_rows(nn_results)


```

```{r}
set.seed(2024)
```

```{r}
fold_metrics_nn <- fold_metrics_nn |> mutate(model = "multinomial")
fold_metrics_rf <- fold_metrics_rf |> mutate(model = "RF")
fold_metrics_svm <- fold_metrics_svm |> mutate(model = "SVM")

all_fold_metrics <- rbind(fold_metrics_nn, fold_metrics_rf, fold_metrics_svm)

summary_stats <- all_fold_metrics |> 
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -c(Resample, model),
    names_to = "metric",
    values_to = "value"
  ) |>
  group_by(model, metric) |>
  summarise(
    n = sum(!is.na(value)),
    Mean = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    Median = median(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    Min = min(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    Q1 = quantile(value, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    Q3 = quantile(value, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    IQR = IQR(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    Max = max(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    SE = SD / sqrt(n),
    CI_lower = Mean - qt(0.975, df = n - 1) * SE,
    CI_upper = Mean + qt(0.975, df = n - 1) * SE,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) 

summary_stats |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = metric, values_from = c(Mean, SD, Median, Min, Q1, Q3, IQR, Max, SE, CI_lower, CI_upper))

bx_plot_summary_stats <- summary_stats |>
  pivot_longer(cols = -c(model, metric, n), names_to = "statistic") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = model, y = value, fill = model, color = model)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = .5) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_jitter() +
  facet_wrap(~metric) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#5bc0be", "#6d52f3", "#d264b6")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#84ffc9", "#aab2ff", "#eca0ff")) +
  theme_classic()
  
ggsave("/home/sofia/Projects/DNM1L/plots/average/bx_plot_summary_stats.png", bx_plot_summary_stats, width = 12, height = 8, units = "in")

```
